- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction, especially in early forecast horizon.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates or ignores downside risk; increase forecast floor or add conservative downward adjustment.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > 3x recent mean), model frequently overcorrects or overshoots; apply smoothing or decay factor to reduce peak forecasts.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; introduce sentiment-triggered mean reversion rule to pull forecasts toward recent history.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early periods (days 1–7) when sentiment is volatile; reduce early forecast weights or apply exponential decay.
- When sentiment is flat or neutral (0.00–0.33), model tends to drift toward extreme values; constrain forecasts to historical range or use moving average filter.
